taxonomic_note: Accepted as a distinct central-Texas endemic in FNA/ITIS/NatureServe and current regional treatments.
look_here_first: Compare the flower directly with pearl milkvine: it is more bell-shaped, with mostly parallel longitudinal green lines that become netted only near the lobe tips/margins, and the inner corolla surface is visibly hairy.

best_field_traits: stems sparsely hairy to nearly glabrous
deeply cordate opposite leaves, basal lobes often overlapping
pale yellow-green campanulate corolla with darker longitudinal lines
five fleshy corona segments free nearly to base
morphology_keys.milkweed_vine_training: Use fused corolla plus corona/gynostegium and follicle armature; preserve modern genus placement even when older/source labels use Matelea.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Matelea reticulata: M. edwardsensis is less hairy and has a campanulate, longitudinally lined, hairy-inside flower with distinct corona segments; M. reticulata is flat, broadly netted, glabrous inside, and has a reduced corona plus a silvery center. Chthamalia biflora: C. biflora is a low hairy herb with paired dark flowers; M. edwardsensis is a twining vine with pale green lined flowers.
